newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says plans no statement, no news conference.
newsitem.headline: Buba says plans no statement, no news conference.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday that it did not plan to hold a news conference nor make any public statements during the day.
"I can say that we do not plan to hold a news conference or to issue a statement," a Bundesbank spokesman told Reuters in response to an enquiry.
Financial markets had speculated that the German central bank would issue a statement on Thursday on what form its securities repurchase tender, or repo, would take next week.
Traders had speculated this week that the bank might prepare the ground for higher money market rates in defence of the weakening mark.

Markets have speculated the bank may signal higher rates by switching from fixed-rate tenders for securities repurchase agreements, or repos -- at which it sets the rate itself -- to variable-rate tenders, at which the repo rate is determined by the rates at which banks bid for Bundesbank funds.

But the Bundesbank injected more funds than expected into the money market on Wednesday in its weekly repo allocation in what dealers interpreted as a sign it did not want to raise short-term interest rates for the time being.
The central bank added a net 2.6 billion marks ($1.4 billion) at its weekly repo auction -- its principal means of supplying the money market with funds -- at a fixed repo rate of 3.00 percent.

A heavy drain of funds from the money market on Wednesday might have been interpreted as a sign the Bundesbank was preparing it for a return to variable-rate tenders and encouraging banks to bid the repo rate higher next week.

The Bundesbank's last central bank council meeting before its one-month summer break on July 24 took the unusual step of setting fixed-rate repo tenders for just two weeks, even though the council was only due to reconvene after four weeks.

The second of those weekly repo pacts was allocated on Wednesday, leaving markets in the dark as to whether next week's repo tender will be a fixed-rate repo at 3.00 percent, a variable-rate repo, or a fixed-rate repo at a higher rate.
Theoretically, the Bundesbank does not have to say what form the tender will take until it invites bids from banks for repos next Tuesday.
But with markets speculating feverishly about whether the Bundesbank will shift to higher rates, dealers have speculated that the bank may make an announcement sooner.
